_comment: Data for tools/run-watchdog.mjs, checked by bot/tests/run-watchdog.test.mjs. Outside TRUST-31's set: a change here is not a change the owner acknowledges.
ghosts_comment: Runs GitHub will neither cancel, force-cancel nor delete (queued or in_progress for ever; support was asked to purge them on 2026-11-10). They are reported once, as known ghosts, and are never stale. Remove an id when GitHub purges it; a ghost that no longer exists is simply not listed.
silence_comment: No successful run for max_minutes means the workflow is silent. `crons` is what the workflow file schedules; the test fails when a file's cron and this list disagree, and when a bound is under 1.5 x the longest gap the cron leaves, so a cron cannot change without this file being looked at. GitHub delivers this repository's crons only every few hours (measured 2026-11-10 on the last 200 runs: longest gap between successes 10.5 h for ingest and moderation, 6.8 h for detectors, 5.5 h for signer and the index, 32 h for served-set), and the workflow_run wakers fire only when something happened, so the bounds are 1.5 x that, rounded: 16 h ingest and moderation, 12 h coverage, signer, detectors and the index, 36 h served-set and the daily ones. The first bounds proposed (60 and 90 min, 3 h) were red in ordinary quiet stretches. A HUNG run is caught in 30 minutes by the stale rule, not by these.

unwatched.why: weekly, and red by design until the alarm channel exists; its own subject is the channel
first week of the month only; GitHub's 60-day idle rule is its subject, not a silence bound of hours
